previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of type 2 diabetes, neurogenic bladder with chronic indwelling Foley catheter, paraplegia, and polysubstance abuse was admitted for recurrent left flank pain and an intensely itchy rash. She had been discharged recently after treatment for pyelonephritis with cefpodoxime but returned with persistent symptoms. Evaluation revealed pyelonephritis due to multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Enterococcus, confirmed by urine culture. A renal ultrasound showed no abscess or obstruction. She was started on IV meropenem and linezolid for a planned 14-day course. The rash was diagnosed as scabies and treated with permethrin cream, with improvement. Lactic acidosis on admission resolved with IV fluids. Due to her history of narcotic-seeking behavior, pain was managed with acetaminophen and limited oral dilaudid. After extensive counseling on the risks of incomplete antibiotic treatment, including sepsis and death, she chose to leave against medical advice on hospital day 7, having completed only 6 of 14 antibiotic days. She was discharged to extended care with instructions to continue insulin, resume metformin, manage constipation, and monitor for infection recurrence.

no visual deficits

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ woman with diabetes, wheelchair bound,
pyelonephritis.

PICC LINE PLACEMENT

INDICATION:  IV access needed for antibiotics for pyelonephritis.

The procedure was explained to the patient.  A timeout was performed.

RADIOLOGIST:  Dr. ___ performed the procedure.

TECHNIQUE:  Using sterile technique and local anesthesia, the right basilic
vein was punctured under direct ultrasound guidance using a micropuncture set.
Hard copies of ultrasound images were obtained before and immediately after
establishing intravenous access.  A peel-away sheath was then placed over a
guidewire and a double-lumen PICC line measuring 43 cm in length was then
placed through the peel-away sheath with its tip positioned in the SVC under
fluoroscopic guidance.  Position of the catheter was confirmed by a
fluoroscopic spot film of the chest.

The peel-away sheath and guidewire were then removed.  The catheter was
secured to the skin, flushed, and a sterile dressing applied.

The patient tolerated the procedure well.  There were no immediate
complications.

IMPRESSION:  Uncomplicated ultrasound and fluoroscopically guided double-lumen
PICC line placement via the right basilic venous approach.  Final internal
length is 43 cm, with the tip positioned in SVC.  The line is ready to use.
